Triage first-touch (session `session_01LrqnyLhY3kYBBRird4peBT`, 2026-08-24): promoted → `pm:queue` (`domain:ui` kept). Recommendation for the claiming seat, not a ruling: prefer option B (make `computeLookupExpand`'s inner test call `isLookupType`, one relation predicate per package) — it wins on the hard-to-get-wrong axis and keeps #4914's item-9 coverage; it is behaviour-affecting, so it needs its own pin evidence. Option A (delete) is the acceptable fallback if B's evidence doesn't come cheap; either way the outcome is one predicate, not two that agree by coincidence.

## 裁决 — triage: a **recommendation**, explicitly not a ruling

Triage first-touch (`os-zhuang`, 2026-08-24 14:28Z), verbatim:

> promoted → `pm:queue` (`domain:ui` kept). **Recommendation for the claiming seat, not a ruling:** prefer option B (make `computeLookupExpand`'s inner test call `isLookupType`, one relation predicate per package) — it wins on the hard-to-get-wrong axis and keeps #4914's item-9 coverage; it is behaviour-affecting, so it needs its own pin evidence. Option A (delete) is the acceptable fallback if B's evidence doesn't come cheap; **either way the outcome is one predicate, not two that agree by coincidence.**

The binding part is the last clause: **one predicate**. B is preferred, A is the fallback.

## What I measured from this seat, so you start from facts not from the card

`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectDataTable.tsx`, inside `computeLookupExpand` (~:226):

```
const isLookup = (t: unknown) => {
  if (typeof t === 'string' && isRetiredFieldType(t)) { reportRetiredFieldType(t); return false; }
  return EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES.has(t as string);
};
```

`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/recordFields.tsx:276`:

```
export function isLookupType(t: unknown): boolean {
  if (typeof t === 'string' && isRetiredFieldType(t)) { reportRetiredFieldType(t); return false; }
  return EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES.has(t as string);
}
```

⚠️ **Those two bodies appear identical.** Verify that yourself on your merge-base — but if it holds, it drives everything below.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. ⛔ **If the bodies are identical, then B is behaviour-PRESERVING, and triage's "it is behaviour-affecting" does not describe it.** That is not a licence to skip evidence — it is a warning that **the ordinary ablation has nothing to show.** A refactor with no observable delta ⛔ cannot be pinned by a behaviour test: a test asserting `computeLookupExpand` still expands `tree` and still refuses `reference` passes **identically** before and after your change, which makes it a **phantom** with respect to this card. ✅ Pin **identity** instead — the same lesson #6068 landed on today: assert that `computeLookupExpand` routes through `isLookupType` rather than through a body of its own, at the source level, because a byte-identical local copy satisfies every behavioural assertion you can write. State in your report which of your assertions would still pass if you reverted the change, and delete or re-aim any that would.
2. ⚠️ **There is one genuine behavioural surface where B might not be a no-op: `reportRetiredFieldType`.** Both predicates call it. If that reporter de-duplicates its warning (per call site, per process, per type — measure which), routing two callers through one function can change **how many times a warning is emitted**, even though the boolean answers never change. ✅ Measure the reporter's de-dup key before you claim B is observationally free, and say what you found. If it does change, that is a real delta and belongs in the changeset.
3. ⚠️ **The card says `isLookupType` has "no production consumer" — that is true, and incomplete.** `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/expandableFamily.identity-5692.test.ts:52` imports it, and that suite is #4914's item-9 coverage which triage explicitly wants **kept**. So under **A** you would have to delete or rewrite that coverage; under **B** the function gains its first production consumer and the suite keeps working. ✅ That asymmetry is the strongest argument for B and belongs in your report, whichever way you go.
4. ⚠️ **Check whether `isLookupType` is re-exported from the package index before you consider A.** If `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` publishes it, option A is a **published-surface removal**: it needs a zero-importer measurement with a counter-probe *including the sibling `objectstack` checkout*, the in-repo-zero-is-not-npm-zero caveat named in the changeset, and a `minor` bump — a materially bigger card than B. ⛔ If you find yourself heading that way, **stop and report** rather than converting this card into that one on your own.
5. **Version policy:** `patch` if nothing published moves (the B shape); **`minor`** if a public export changes; ⛔ **never `major`** — `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses it outright (AGENTS.md §版本号策略).

## PM建议路线

Take **B**. It is triage's preference, it keeps the coverage, it avoids the published-removal question entirely, and — per assumption 1 — its evidence *is* cheap once you stop trying to get it from a behaviour test and pin identity instead. ✅ If your measurement contradicts any of the above and A becomes the right call, say so with the evidence and ⛔ do not silently switch.

## Verification

Predict the direction **before** running. Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and, separately**, the removed text — for this card that means the local `isLookup` body is *gone* from `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and the call to `isLookupType` is *present*, each grepped on its own. ⚠️ Print the landing site; ⚠️ assert anchor uniqueness before writing (⛔ these two function bodies are near-identical text — an anchor matching both is exactly the failure mode measured on #5927 this round, where one anchor hit three sites on byte-identical lines); ⚠️ restore any probe under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command and confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty. Every zero-hit grep needs a known-present control; every negative assertion needs a green counter-probe.

**Gates by name, with exit codes:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red — `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` — from the **missing-`node_modules`** red), root-form vitest over `packages/plugin-dashboard/src` (⚠️ include `expandableFamily.identity-5692.test.ts` explicitly and quote its per-test names, so a suite that silently stopped matching cannot read as green), the downstream **prefix-form** sweep `pnpm --filter '...@object-ui/plugin-dashboard' <script>` with the contract direction stated, and eslint with merge-base delta (⚠️ plain `eslint .`; ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`). Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing — ⚠️ **#6073 landed today and widened that gate's notion of a package's source** beyond `/src/`.

⚠️ **Standing rule from #5874 this round:** derive your gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**, ⛔ not from top-level script names — `check:esm-specifiers` runs as a step inside the `Type Check` job under a name that does not read like one, and that class of miss turned a PR red today. Run `pnpm check:esm-specifiers` if you add or move any relative import in a published package (an import added to `ObjectDataTable.tsx` counts).

## Deliverable

Draft PR, body with `Fixes #5876`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — they render as HTML and vanish) and return it. State, per gate: command, exit code, what a red would have meant; which option you took and why; the measured answer to each of assumptions 1–4; and — explicitly — **which of your assertions would still pass if the change were reverted**.

## Measured answers to PM assumptions 1–4

**1 — bodies identical, so B is behaviour-PRESERVING.** Confirmed on merge-base `7c96c9420`: the two bodies are the same code line-for-line (the local one carried an extra comment). Triage's "it is behaviour-affecting" does not describe this change. Consequence taken seriously rather than worked around: no behavioural test can pin it, so none was written. The pin is identity in two halves that fail for different reasons — a `vi.doMock` double observing `computeLookupExpand` actually CALL `isLookupType` in both column modes, and a comments-stripped source read proving no second body survives for it to call instead. The source half matters because the call half alone can pass while a dead copy still sits in the file.

**2 — `reportRetiredFieldType` de-dup key: per SPELLING, module-global.** Measured in `packages/core/src/utils/retired-field-types.ts`: one module-level `const reportedRetiredTypes = new Set<string>()`, keyed on the spelling, with the source comment "the dedupe is per SPELLING, not per face". Both predicates already imported that same module instance, so they already shared the Set. Routing two callers through one function therefore cannot change how many times a warning is emitted. B is observationally free on this surface too — had the key been per call site, this would have been a real delta and would have belonged in the changeset.

**3 — the "no production consumer" reading is true but incomplete.** Two test files import `isLookupType`, not one: `expandableFamily.identity-5692.test.ts:52` and `lookupTypes.retiredFieldType.test.ts:37` (the latter is #4914's item-9 coverage, 8 tests). The asymmetry is real and it is the strongest argument for B: under A both would have needed deleting or rewriting, under B the function gains its first production consumer and both suites keep working untouched — verified by running them, both green.

**4 — `isLookupType` is NOT on the published surface.** `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx` exports only the components, `CONFIG_PANEL_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS` / `useConfigPanelTranslation`, and the `dataset-catalog` types; `recordFields` is never re-exported. So option A would **not** have been a published-surface removal — a smaller card than the dispatch feared. That did not change the decision: B was still right on the "one predicate" clause and on keeping the item-9 coverage, and it avoids the zero-importer/npm-reach question entirely. `patch`, not `minor`; never `major`.

## Deviations worth PM attention

- Two commits, not one. The second fixes a flaw the first ablation leg exposed in my own pin (control and subject assertions indistinguishable). Reported rather than squashed away, because the near-miss is the useful part.
- The downstream sweep's first run was red on an unbuilt closure, and the counter-probe (build `examples/**`, re-run, green, diff unchanged) is what makes the green readable. Both runs are recorded above rather than only the green one.
- CI convergence not awaited, per the standing contract — the PR was opened draft and this report filed at that moment. PR is **draft**, not enqueued, no auto-merge. `mergeable_state: behind` at report time; `main` moved to `0c282d979` while gates ran.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, enqueued

PR **#6099** at `42c38c2a4`. Gates read **once** at 17:09:30Z, off this run's own `started_at` (16:56:19Z). **22 checks, 19 success + 3 skipped, 0 failing, 0 still running.** Not a governed surface; marked ready and enqueued. ⛔ Nothing merged by hand. (`mergeable_state: behind` at report time is expected — the merge queue rebases.)

**Option B**, triage's preference, taken. `computeLookupExpand` no longer carries its own `isLookup`; it calls `isLookupType` at both call sites, and `ObjectDataTable.tsx` no longer imports `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`, `isRetiredFieldType` or `reportRetiredFieldType` at all. **The package now holds one relation predicate**, which is the clause triage said binds either way.

### The identity-vs-behaviour call was the card

Verified on merge-base `7c96c9420` that the two bodies were **identical**, so **B is behaviour-preserving** and triage's *"it is behaviour-affecting"* does not describe it. ✅ That is not a licence to skip evidence, it is the reason the pin had to be on **identity** — and the report answers the question the dispatch actually asked:

> **Which of your assertions would still pass on a revert?** — every pre-existing assertion in all four describes of `expandableFamily.identity-5692.test.ts`, and all 8 tests in `lookupTypes.retiredFieldType.test.ts`. **All 18 passed under ablation, by measurement.** They are **controls** with respect to this card, ⛔ not pins of it, and the file's header docblock now says so. Exactly **two** assertions fail on a revert, and they are the two new ones.

That is the whole difference between a refactor that is pinned and one that merely has tests near it.

### The ablation found a flaw in the pin itself

⚠️ The first leg failed on its **control** line — *"probe stripped the code away"* — which is **the exact message a broken probe would give**, making a real revert and a broken probe indistinguishable. A control that cannot survive the mutation is not a control.

✅ Fixed in a second commit: controls are now text present in **both** versions of the file (`out.add(acc)`), and the `isLookupType` call count moved to the **subject**. The re-run then failed with honest subject messages — *"explicit whitelist answered the relation question without asking isLookupType"* and *"computeLookupExpand stopped calling the shared predicate"*. Predicted direction (both new pins red, every pre-existing test green) then observed exactly: `Tests 2 failed | 18 passed (20)`.

This is the **third** phantom-class defect self-caught in this round, and all three share one root: *an assertion or control that cannot distinguish the two states of the world.* Worth naming as a class.

### Two assumptions came back different — both cheaper than I priced them

- ⚠️ **Assumption 4 was a false alarm.** `isLookupType` is **not** re-exported from `index.tsx`, so option A would **not** have been a published-surface removal. ✅ Did not change the decision — B still wins on the "one predicate" clause and on keeping #4914's item-9 coverage — but the fallback was cheaper than the dispatch feared, and saying so is more useful than letting the warning stand uncorrected.
- ⚠️ **Assumption 2 resolved cleanly in B's favour.** `reportRetiredFieldType` dedupes **per spelling**, in a single module-level Set inside `@object-ui/core` that **both bodies already shared** — so warning-emission count cannot move. ✅ Nothing behavioural to put in the changeset, measured rather than assumed.

And item-9 coverage was kept **by execution, not by claim**: `lookupTypes.retiredFieldType.test.ts` ran green with all 8 tests named.

### Readings worth keeping

⚠️ The downstream prefix sweep went **red (exit 2)** on its first run with `Cannot find module '@object-ui/example-schema-catalog'` — the **unbuilt-closure** class, because only `./packages/**` had been built. Building `./examples/**` flipped it green **with the diff unchanged**, which is the counter-probe that it was environmental. ✅ Diagnosed rather than reported as a failure — and I have added "build `./examples/**` too" to subsequent dispatches.

Direction demonstrated rather than asserted: prefix form = the package **and its dependents**, `Scope: 7 of 47 workspace projects`, all 7 `Done`.

`pnpm lint` was run **repo-wide, not narrowed** (47/47 tasks), so no narrowing declaration is owed. `renderFieldValue` was deliberately left in place because #6014 reads that seam — ✅ the serial fence held without needing to be enforced.
